paragraphReviews.judgment: A single continuous channel greeting opens a concrete equipment/appearance-time question; EN preserves the same viewer experience and spoken KO has no extra greeting.
Benefit and route are visible results, easier selection/testing, then appearance enjoyment. The overview promises only content later covered, and EN/spoken KO retain that order.
First-example bridge now names Raiders equipment choice and a real test range; no shop/purchase, S3 lobby or same-gun replacement is promised.

Raiders ink-combat/treasure context, mechanical gadgets and test range are introduced in plain terms. Peer primary-source report supports these broad facts; the actual bank proves gadget equip then use, without needing a main-gun swap.

Conditional general example: numbers alone may not convey reach/spread/sequence. It does not claim all three patterns were measured in Raiders; visuals must use observed qualitative effects or an explicitly authored diagram.
Observation points are selected equipment and actual test targets. No invented two-ship/right-hand-shop reference remains. EN uses the player rather than attributing the captured action to us.

Preview is explained as showing the decision-relevant result. EN before-committing is interpreted as before the final choice/use in a raid, not before equip/purchase; source editing must not assert a pre-purchase feature.
Visible differences lead to reasons to choose; the universally dominant weapon is a conditional design example, not an allegation about Raiders balance.
General choice criteria inherit the preceding visible-attack differences. The removed ACVI and S3 Shooter/Charger specifics do not survive in any language.
Trade-off is explicitly defined as linked benefit and sacrifice. Damage per shot and interval are introduced as criteria, with no measured Raiders stat or unsupported gear limitation.
Fictional A100/2s and B40/0.5s lead to long-run averages50 and80 damage per second. Spoken aliases preserve every number and the A/B assignment.

One shot against90 health explains why100 damage can be preferable to40. KO/EN/spoken explicitly call the values illustrative, exclude misses/armor, and do not convert the long-run result to a universal ranking.
Distinct strengths/unfavorable situations are retained, then the concrete remaining problem becomes finding desired equipment among more combinations.
Canonical BOTW title is retained and categories/icons distinguish item types. Actual Materials→Shields→Weapons navigation supports this; no sort execution or resistance effect is asserted.

Icon means a small type-identifying picture; similar shapes require names/functions too. Armor is a general readability example and has existing independent BOTW armor-menu support, not proof from the new weapon/material bank alone.
ACNH initial appearance categories change options and preview the chosen appearance on the avatar. Initial creation is explicit; no mirror, shop, later unlock or clothing interaction is added.

Sorting is defined as changing order by a criterion and explicitly switches to an illustrative list. Preferred type is a category need; any worked attack sorting must reorder the same fictional items, not pretend filtering/sorting occurred in BOTW.
Finding candidates still leaves the novice without a starting combination; suggesting that set motivates the next automatic-equipment function.
Automatic equipment is concretely selecting and equipping by a predefined rule, rather than a vague recommendation. No selected commercial game is claimed to implement it.
Strongest is criterion-dependent: combined attack and cold survival may select different sets. This is a conditional design example rather than a measured BOTW armor solution.
An attack-focused authored menu supplies the concrete automatic-equipment operation. All languages disclaim reproducing a particular game and a universal optimum.
A starting set followed by manual edits preserves both convenience and choice; the open need is whether that set feels suitable in use.
Menu expectation versus movement/attack motivates the distance between editing and trial. This follows the preceding hand-feel question directly.

Exact selected BOTW operation is axe selection in quick weapon list→same-area axe visible→tree struck and felled. Native local77–90 corroborates it; no Fuse, dedicated test room, rollback, free trial or stat measurement remains.
Raiders test range provides pre-raid practice. Long travel/battle is an explicitly conditional inconvenience; no claim of free upgrades or costless reset is made.
Change→test→change feedback remains a core claim. It is a general loop supported by Raiders menu→use→return bank, not a claim that the BOTW tree returns to its original state.
The prior performance discussion leaves the precise question whether liking a change requires better performance, preparing appearance-based value.
ACNH face and hairstyle choices express the desired character appearance. No damage/attribute improvement is associated with those choices.
Observed preview updates make preference the outcome rather than damage increase. Same-avatar before/after visuals should expose the changed feature.
Robot versus cute-character preferences are generic illustrative possibilities, not a fourth game example. Unchanged performance can coexist with the enjoyment of appearance choice.
Games may link or separate appearance and performance; the stated requirement is knowing what changes and seeing its outcome. No universal game rule is asserted.

Customization returns as the choosing process as well as a finished result. The established equipment/appearance actions supply the term meaning; first displayed term should pair Customization with a plain Korean definition.
Conclusion recaps visible effects→trade-offs→finding→testing without adding a new claim or reordering the original five considerations.
Appearance need not increase strength; imagining a desired look provides a different enjoyment from combat/movement, preserving the reference conclusion.
What can change and how to choose/check/revise are the final design directions. The viewer question asks for a relevant personal game example without biography/source-creator framing.

mathReview.derivation: Long-run average damage rate = damage per shot / shot interval;100/2=50 and40/0.5=80. A single100-damage hit can defeat90-health target, whereas one40-damage hit cannot.
mathReview.assumptions: Sustained sufficiently long comparison with regular intervals and all shots hitting; startup/finite-window effects, misses, armor and other conditions are not modeled. A lone firing opportunity is a different decision condition.
mathReview.displayGuard: Show fictional weapons and an explicit 설명용 수치 / 가상 무기 label; no actual Raiders/BOTW/ACNH performance measurement or numeric overlay. If using DPS abbreviation, first display 초당 피해량(Damage per Second,DPS) with the division relationship.
mathReview.spokenAliasCheck: A→에이,B→비,100→백,2초→이 초,40→사십,0.5초→영 점 오초,50→오십,80→팔십,90→구십; textual meaning matches. Actual pronunciation is pending.
